title: Safeguards to Ensure Citizen Data Is Not Disclosed to or Processed by Foreign-headquartered Vendors
what_it_is: Safeguards to Ensure Citizen Data Is Not Disclosed to or Processed by Foreign-headquartered Vendors

sections.label: Safeguards for citizen data with vendors
sections.summary: The Government applies risk-based safeguards, technical controls, governance and contracts to protect citizen data used by vendors from foreign disclosure demands.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Digital Development and Information (a) whether the whole-of-Government data architecture permits proprietary artificial intelligence (AI) or data analytics platforms from foreign-headquartered vendors to process citizen data; and (b) if so, what legal and technical safeguards ensure that such data cannot be compelled for disclosure by a foreign government under that government's domestic laws.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: We have established comprehensive safeguards to protect citizen data when working with any vendor.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: Our risk-based approach ensures that data access is granted strictly on a "needs-basis" following the principle of least privilege.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: Vendors are expected to implement robust technical safeguards such as non-retention of data, encryption as well as access and identity management.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: Data residency may also be required, depending on the sensitivity of the data.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: This is coupled with proper governance frameworks and contractual agreements on how the data can be accessed, used, stored and retained.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: These help to prevent vendors from accessing, using or disclosing government data where they are not permitted to do so, including in response to demands from foreign governments.

sections.label: Foreign laws can override contracts
sections.summary: Some jurisdictions' laws with extraterritorial reach can override contractual obligations, so the Government also relies on technical controls and governance frameworks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: Legal and contractual agreements aside, the reality is that no matter what legal provisions the contracts may contain, some jurisdictions like, as he mentioned, the US, may have legislation or regulations, including with extraterritorial reach, that empower government agencies to require companies or entities within their jurisdictions to provide certain information.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: Such legislation or regulations can override contractual obligations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: This is why the Government's approach is to rely not solely on contractual provisions, but also on other risk mitigation measures, which I have mentioned, such as technical controls and safeguards as well as governance frameworks, which limit what use cases and categories of information may be used with non-government provided tools and platforms.
